core_obligations: Reduce to products and equalizers and quote the product case (proof lines 2852-2855).
Set up the equalizer diagram of henselian pairs (proof lines 2856-2860).
Show that every element of one plus the limit ideal is a unit, so that the limit ideal lies in the Jacobson radical (proof lines 2862-2868).
Take the polynomial of the shape required by Gabber's criterion and note that its image in the first ring has a unique root near one, and likewise in the second (proof lines 2869-2879).
Use uniqueness of that root to show the two images agree, so the root descends to the equalizer and the criterion is met (proof lines 2880-2882).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to products and equalizers (proof lines 2852-2855).
Put the limit ideal in the Jacobson radical (proof lines 2862-2868).
Descend the root of the polynomial by uniqueness (proof lines 2869-2882).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an inverse limit of henselian pairs, with the limit ideal, is again a henselian pair. The proof reduces to products and equalizers since limits in the relevant category are built from those, quotes the product case, and then treats an equalizer diagram of henselian pairs. The verification uses Gabber's criterion: elements of one plus the limit ideal are units because inverses are unique and the statement holds in the first pair, which puts the limit ideal inside the Jacobson radical, and then a polynomial of the shape used in the criterion, whose coefficients apart from the leading ones lie in the limit ideal, has a unique root near one in the first ring, whose images under the two parallel maps agree by uniqueness, so that root descends to the equalizer.
